![A Doric temple overlaid with formal measurements and proportions. Image from [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/17/pramaana-labs-raises-27-million-seed-round-from-khosla-ventures-to-bring-formal-verification-to-ai/).](cover.jpg){fig-align="center"}

[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/17/pramaana-labs-raises-27-million-seed-round-from-khosla-ventures-to-bring-formal-verification-to-ai/) reports that [Pramaana Labs](https://pramaanalabs.ai/) has raised a $27M seed round led by [Khosla Ventures](https://www.khoslaventures.com/) to apply formal verification, specifically the [Lean](https://lean-lang.org/) proof language used to check mathematical proofs, as a deterministic layer on top of an LLM. The LLM still answers the natural-language question. A Lean-style system then checks that the answer obeys a formalized rulebook. Pramaana is targeting rule-dense, high-stakes verticals like law, tax preparation, and drug discovery, building a separate verification system per domain with oversight from experts such as former IRS commissioner [Danny Werfel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Werfel). The company was founded by three IIT Madras alumni whose backgrounds run through Google Maps moderation, [Glean](https://www.glean.com/), and [Google DeepMind](https://deepmind.google/)'s Gemini team. Co-founder [Ranjan Rajagopalan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ranjan-rajagopalan/) frames the bet this way: "The world's hardest problems are not unsolvable. They are unformalized."

What Pramaana is building:

- **The verification stack.** A Domain Formalizer converts regulatory, statutory, and scientific text into machine-checkable specifications, capturing definitions, conditions, exceptions, and dependencies. Provers and solvers then return proof artifacts, proofs, counterexamples, and traceable explanations, showing which rule was used and where the answer follows or fails.
- **Tax first.** The opening vertical formalizes tax rules for compliance, advisory, and policy simulation, with legal compliance, clinical safety, software and protocol correctness, and public policy named as later targets.
- **An outside-research arm.** A fellowship, [Project 1729](https://pramaanalabs.ai/), invites external teams to formalize high-stakes domains, offering funding, compute, and an embedded Pramaana engineer.

## My Notes

- **The bottleneck moves from the model to the spec.** The deterministic layer checks that the LLM's output obeys a formalized rulebook, but it cannot check that the rulebook itself is correct or complete. A proof of conformance is only as good as the formalization, and turning law or tax into Lean means making thousands of interpretive choices that can each be wrong. [Verified Doesn't Mean Nothing Can Go Wrong](/posts/20260413-verified-not-safe/) is the direct caution here: a Claude agent found a buffer overflow in the Lean runtime under code that was itself formally verified.

- **The verticals are rule-dense, but not equally formalizable.** Law and tax are good fits because they are written rules, and France's [CATALA](https://catala-lang.org/) project already turns much of the French tax and benefit code into executable form. Drug discovery is a harder case: much of it is empirical and statistical rather than a codified rulebook, so the pitch that codifying the rules makes the reasoning deterministic fits tax far better than it fits biology. The ongoing cost is also real, since a formalization of the tax code has to be re-checked every time the code changes.

- **This is a per-domain build, not a horizontal product.** Each vertical gets its own Lean-style system overseen by domain experts: a former IRS commissioner for tax, named professors for cybersecurity and drug discovery. The defensibility comes from the formalization work and the expert relationships, which reads closer to a high-end services model than to software that scales by adding users. The Project 1729 fellowship, which embeds a Pramaana engineer with each outside team, fits that shape: each new domain is its own formalization project. The same LLM-plus-Lean toolchain is being pushed on open math problems in [Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search](/posts/20260606-ai-formal-proof-search/), where the binding constraint is likewise how much gets formalized, not the model.

- **The competitive landscape, especially in law and tax.** The field splits on what makes a high-stakes answer trustworthy, and Pramaana's wager is on machine-checkable proof:
  - **The proof camp** (Pramaana's own): **[Axiom](/posts/20260514-carina-hong-axiom-math-is-agi/)**, founder Carina Hong's Lean-based startup, runs the same deterministic-formal-layer thesis aimed at mathematics. **[Imandra](https://www.imandra.ai/)** sells "reasoning as a service," applying automated reasoning and formal verification to mission-critical and financial-regulatory decisions, which puts it closest to Pramaana's professional territory.
  - **The retrieval camp** (what Pramaana positions against): X's **[Moonshot for Specialized Professional Intelligence](https://x.company/blog/posts/moonshot-for-professional-intelligence/)** and **[Harvey](https://www.harvey.ai/)** chase the legal market with LLM analysis over private documents, while **[Thomson Reuters and LexisNexis](/posts/20240531-legal-ai-hallucinations/)** tools still hallucinate more than 17% of the time. In tax, **[Black Ore](https://www.blackore.ai/)**'s "Tax Autopilot" automates tax preparation for CPA (certified public accountant) firms with a claimed 99% accuracy, and France's CATALA remains the closest formal precedent.
